chunks: And of the people is he whose speech pleases you in worldly life, and he calls God to witness concerning what is in his heart, yet he is the most contentious of opponents.
ai.seo_question: What characterizes the person whose speech pleases us but is actually contentious?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse characterizes the 'munafiq' (hypocrite) whose eloquence masks inner corruption, a trait highlighted by Al-Tabarsi as a warning against being swayed by rhetorical skill over substantive truth. The description of him as 'alad al-khisam' (most stubborn in argument) underscores the spiritual danger of self-deception, where one's own heart becomes the primary witness to a sincerity that is ultimately illusory.
